grammar.title: 信息疑问句
rows: 疑问词 + 助动词 + 主语 + 动词原形；be 动词直接提前。
grammar.tip: 询问主语时不用 do：Who lives here? Whose 表示“谁的”，which 表示限定范围中的选择。
grammar.say: Where did you grow up?

grammar.title: 间接疑问句
rows: 礼貌开头 + 疑问词/if + 主语 + 谓语。
Can you tell me where Leo lives?
你能告诉我利奥住在哪里吗？
grammar.tip: 从句用陈述语序，不说 where does Leo live；一般疑问句转为 if/whether 从句。
grammar.say: Can you tell me where Leo lives?

pron.title: 新信息重音
pron.explain: 回答问题时突出新信息。已知信息轻读，纠正时重读被纠正部分。

grammarQuiz.why: 间接问句的从句使用主语＋谓语。
Whose 询问物品属于谁。
Who 是主语，动词直接用第三人称单数。

grammarQuiz.q: Do you know ___ she is married?
grammarQuiz.why: 是否已婚是一般疑问，用 if 引导。

writingTask.title: 给海外亲属写认识彼此的邮件
writingTask.task: 用 100～140 词介绍生活、性格和兴趣，并问对方两个问题。
writingTask.focus: 每段一个主题：联系缘由、个人介绍、提问与结尾。
writingTask.model:
Hi Anna,

I'm your cousin Wei. Your father gave me your address. I live in Seattle with my family, and I'm taking an English class. My friends say I'm cheerful and reliable, although I can be nervous with new people.

I'm into photography and walking. Could you tell me what you enjoy doing? I wonder if you still play basketball. I'd love to learn more about your life.

Best,
Wei

readings.title: A cousin in Seattle
readings.text:
Hi Leo,

I’m your cousin Wei. Your mother gave me your email address. I was born in Chengdu and raised there, but I now live in Seattle with my family. I’m studying English and volunteering at a community garden.

My friends say I’m reliable and helpful. I’m sometimes nervous when I meet new people, so gardening gives me something to talk about. I’m also into photography. Last weekend I took pictures of our cheerful volunteers.

Could you tell me what you enjoy doing? I wonder if you still play the guitar. My sister says you have a generous friend who teaches music. How do you know him?

I’d love to hear about your life in Portland. Maybe we can meet during the summer.

Best,
Wei

readings.text:
WANTED: A SMALL DIGITAL CAMERA

I’m looking for a used camera for a community photography class in Seattle. I don’t need a fancy one, but it must work well and be easy to carry. A plain black model would be fine.

I’ve already checked several stores, but I haven’t found an affordable one yet. Most of the cameras I’ve seen are brand new. Older ones are welcome if they are in good condition. Please don’t offer one with a damaged screen.

I need a charger and enough storage for a day of pictures. If you have a suitable camera, please send photos and tell me how long you’ve had it. I can collect it on Saturday. Please contact me through this community website.

readings.title: Help visitors find their way
readings.text:
RIVER CENTER NEEDS VOLUNTEERS

Our small visitor center near the waterfront is looking for friendly people to help on weekends. Visitors often ask about bus routes, ferry departures, local sculptures, and places to stay. You don’t have to know every answer, but you should be willing to check reliable information.

Volunteers work in pairs. Before your first shift, an experienced volunteer will show you the maps and explain the booking system. You should be comfortable speaking to people and giving clear directions. Another language is useful, but it isn’t essential.

The center is beside the public parking lot. To reach the office, enter the lobby and take the stairs to the second floor. Send a short personal statement explaining why you would like to help.

河畔中心招募志愿者

志愿者两人一组工作。第一次值班前，有经验的志愿者会介绍地图和预订系统。你应乐于与人交流，能够清楚指路。会另一种语言有帮助，但不是必要条件。
中心在公共停车场旁。进入大厅，上楼到二楼办公室。请发送简短个人陈述，说明为什么想来帮忙。

readings.text:
Hi everyone,

Here is our plan for Saturday’s microadventure in Portland. First, we’re meeting outside the library at nine. Please bring a raincoat and a reusable bottle. I think the riverside walk will be relaxing, but the forecast suggests rain.

Next, we’re taking the bus to the bridge. Maya has checked the route, and Leo is dealing with the tickets. After the walk, we’re having lunch at the covered market. Finally, we’re visiting a small museum nearby.

If the rain is heavy, we’ll skip the walk and go straight to the museum. There’s no need to worry about the change. At least we have an indoor option. Please let me know by Friday if you’re coming.

See you,
Wei

writingTask.title: 写一个真实的小故事
writingTask.task: 用 120～160 词讲一次丢失物品或获得帮助的经历，包含背景、转折、结果和感受。

checklist: 使用过去时与过去进行时
writingTask.model:
Last Friday, I was waiting for a bus when I found a phone on the bench. At first, I didn't know what to do. Then it rang.

I answered, and the owner asked where I was. She was searching for the phone at a café nearby. Ten minutes later, she arrived at the bus stop. She was grateful and offered to buy me coffee.

readings.book: 第3册 5.4 目标对应原创材料
readings.title: Make a small story interesting
readings.text:
You don’t need a dramatic adventure to tell a good story. A small mistake can be interesting if listeners understand why it mattered. Start with a place and a time, then explain what you were doing.

For example, imagine waiting for a bus in Seattle when you notice a wallet on the sidewalk. Don’t immediately say that you returned it. First, describe the problem: there is no phone number inside, and your bus is arriving. What did you decide to do?

Next, tell the events in order. Use words such as suddenly, later, and finally, but don’t put them in every sentence. End with the result and how you felt. A surprising detail can help, but a true story should stay true.
readings.zh:
不必有惊险冒险才能讲好故事。只要听者理解事情为什么重要，小错误也会有趣。先交代地点时间，再说明当时在做什么。
比如你在西雅图等公交，看到人行道上有个钱包。不要马上说归还了，先交代难题：里面没有电话，公交又来了。你决定怎么做？
然后按顺序讲事件，可用 suddenly、later、finally，但不必每句都用。结尾说明结果和感受。意外细节有帮助，但真实故事应保持真实。

readings.title: More than a delivery shortcut
readings.text:
I enjoyed your podcast about city deliveries, but I’m not sure drones are the best answer for our neighborhood. There is already a lot of noise, and the apartments have very little outdoor space. Where will the packages land?

If deliveries arrive at a shared collection point, drivers will make fewer stops. That could reduce traffic on our narrow street. People could collect their packages while walking home. What about residents who cannot carry heavy items, though? They will still need delivery to their doors.

I think we should test a small project before changing the whole system. If the organizers listen carefully to residents, they’ll learn which problems matter most. A useful plan should help people, not just move packages faster.

readings.book: 第3册 7.4 目标对应原创材料
readings.title: Animation beyond childhood
readings.text:
Some adults think animated movies are only for children. That idea misses what animation can do. A drawn city can change shape, an animal can explain a difficult feeling, and a silent scene can tell a story without any dialogue.

In our Seattle film club, we recently watched a fictional short film called The Paper Bridge. A young musician builds a bridge from old concert posters to visit a lonely neighbor. Children in the audience enjoyed the colorful journey. Adults talked about loneliness and the way music connects people.

Not every animated movie works for every age, of course. Some stories are frightening, and some jokes depend on adult experience. Before choosing one for a family evening, read a description and consider the audience. Animation is a way of making a film, not a guarantee that it is suitable for children.
readings.zh:
有些成年人认为动画只属于孩子，这忽略了动画的表现力。画出来的城市能改变形状，动物能解释复杂感受，无对白场景也能讲故事。
西雅图电影社最近看了一部虚构短片《纸桥》。年轻音乐家用旧演出海报搭桥，去看望孤独的邻居。孩子喜欢多彩旅程，成年人讨论孤独和音乐如何连接人。
当然，不是所有动画都适合所有年龄。有些故事吓人，有些笑话依赖成年人的经历。家庭观影前应看简介、考虑观众。动画是一种制作方式，并不保证适合儿童。

writingTask.task: 用 120～150 词描述最近尝试的习惯、持续时间、成果与下一步。
writingTask.focus: 用 for the last week、recently、before、next week 等表达清楚时间关系。
checklist: 承认限制并提出下一步
writingTask.model:
For the last two weeks, I've been preparing my study materials before going to bed. Before this change, I wasted time searching for books every morning.

So far, I've finished four reading tasks and started each session on time. I still get distracted sometimes, but I can concentrate more easily when everything is ready.

Next week, I'll try leaving my phone in another room. I don't want a perfect schedule. I want a routine that I can keep.

readings.book: 第3册 8.4 目标对应原创材料
readings.title: A twenty-minute experiment
readings.text:
After listening to a podcast about time management, I tried one small change. For the last week, I’ve been leaving my phone in the kitchen while I study at my desk. I work for twenty minutes, then take a short break.

Before this experiment, I often spent an hour looking at a page without understanding it. Messages interrupted me, and I kept starting again. This week I’ve completed three reading assignments and prepared one presentation. I haven’t become faster at everything, but I can concentrate more easily.

The routine doesn’t work perfectly every day. On Tuesday I had to help my brother, so I stopped early. That wasn’t a failure. I’m learning to make realistic plans instead of filling every minute. Next week I’ll try preparing my materials the night before.
readings.zh:
听完时间管理播客后，我尝试一个小改变：过去一周，坐书桌前学习时把手机放在厨房。学习二十分钟，再短暂休息。
以前常盯着一页看一个小时也没理解，消息不断打断，让我反复重来。本周完成了三项阅读作业和一次演示准备。我并非做什么都变快了，但更容易专注。
不是每天都完美。周二需要帮助弟弟，就提前结束了，这不算失败。我在学着制定现实计划，而不是填满每分钟。下周打算前一晚准备材料。

readings.text:
JOB: WEEKEND LIBRARY ASSISTANT

A fictional community library in Seattle needs an assistant for Saturday mornings. Applicants must be comfortable helping visitors and using a computer. You don’t need a university degree, but you must be reliable. The assistant will organize materials, explain basic computer tasks, and help at events.

APPLICANT: MAYA CHEN
Education: Community college, currently studying education.
Experience: Volunteer at a neighborhood center, September to June. Helped visitors complete forms and organized weekly activities.
Skills: Speaks English and Mandarin; uses spreadsheets; explains instructions clearly.
Availability: Saturday mornings and some weekday evenings.

Maya’s experience matches several requirements, but her application should still explain why she wants this particular role. A résumé is most useful when its details relate to the job. It should give accurate evidence, not a long list of unsupported claims.

I bought the Clear Day glass bottle two weeks ago. It is easy to clean, and the simple design fits well in my bag. Although glass is heavier than plastic, I like being able to see how much water is left.

writingTask.title: 写挑战自己的经历

starters: If I tried again, I would …
writingTask.model:
Last month, I gave my first short talk at a community meeting. At first, I thought I would forget everything. I practiced with a friend and wrote down three main points.

In fact, I forgot only one sentence. I paused and explained the idea in simpler words. Two neighbors asked useful questions afterwards.

readings.book: 第3册 11.4 目标对应原创材料
readings.title: A challenge small enough to try
readings.text:
Leaving your comfort zone doesn’t have to mean taking a dangerous risk. For Wei, it meant speaking for two minutes at a community meeting in Seattle. He usually stayed quiet, although he had useful ideas.

Before the meeting, he wrote down three points and practiced with a friend. His goal wasn’t to impress everyone. It was to explain one suggestion clearly. During the talk, he forgot a sentence, paused, and continued in simpler words. Afterwards, two neighbors asked questions about his idea.

Wei learned that preparation could make an unfamiliar task manageable. If he tried a longer talk, he would prepare in the same way and ask for feedback. He wouldn’t begin with a huge audience. Small challenges allow people to learn from mistakes without risking everything. Success can mean doing something imperfectly and discovering that you can improve.

会前他写下三点并和朋友练习。目标不是让所有人赞叹，而是清楚解释一个建议。发言时他忘了一句，停顿后改用简单说法继续。之后两位邻居来问他的想法。

grammar.title: 不定代词
rows: someone/anyone/no one/everyone 指人；something/anything/nothing/everything 指物，通常接单数动词。
Everyone is ready, but something is missing.
大家都准备好了，但少了点东西。
grammar.tip: 修饰语放后面：something interesting。标准英语避免双重否定：I didn’t see anything。

grammar.title: 间接引语
rows: 过去报告动词后，时态常后移：is→was，will→would，can→could，过去/完成→had done。
She said that she was tired. He said he would help.
她说她累了。他说他会帮忙。
grammar.tip: 根据叙述视角调整人称和时间词；仍然有效的事实可不后移。tell 通常需要人作宾语。

writingTask.title: 写一个生活教训趣事
writingTask.task: 用 130～170 词讲一个小事故：经过、感受、别人说的话和学到的教训。
writingTask.focus: 用不同表达避免重复，如 in the end/finally、felt awful/felt miserable；同义表达仍要符合语境。
writingTask.model:
I once left a window open before going out. My friend had warned me about the rain, but I was rushing. When I returned, my blanket was wet. I felt awful.

Leo said that he had an extra blanket, and Maya helped me dry the floor. Nobody blamed me. In the end, we laughed about my unusually fresh bedroom.

Now I check the windows before leaving. I learned to finish one task before starting another.

readings.book: 第3册 12.4 目标对应原创材料
readings.title: The open window
readings.text:
Last month I stayed in a tiny cabin with two friends. The view was magnificent, and I was thrilled to spend a weekend away from the city. Before we went for a walk, Maya told me that rain was expected. I said I would close the windows.

I closed the kitchen window but forgot the one beside my bed. While we were outside, a storm arrived. When we returned, my blanket was wet and the floor was slippery. Nothing expensive was damaged, but I felt miserable and embarrassed.

Leo said that he had brought an extra blanket. Maya helped me dry the floor. Nobody blamed me, although I apologized several times. In the end, we laughed about my very fresh, very wet bedroom. Now I check every window before leaving. A small mistake taught me to finish one task before rushing to the next.
readings.zh:
上个月我和两个朋友住进小木屋，景色壮丽，离城度周末让我很兴奋。出门散步前，玛雅说预报有雨。我答应关窗。
我关了厨房窗，却忘了床边那扇。我们在外时下了暴雨。回来后毯子湿了，地板很滑。没损坏贵重物品，但我难受又尴尬。
利奥说带了备用毯子，玛雅帮我擦地。虽然我道歉多次，没人责怪我。最后我们笑说卧室空气特别新鲜，也特别湿。现在离开前我会检查每扇窗。小错误教会我做完一件事再急着做下一件。

qs.why: 第二段明确床边窗户。
第三段说明备用毯子。

qs.q: What lesson did the writer learn?
opts: Finish one task before starting another.
qs.a: Finish one task before starting another.
qs.why: 结尾直接表达教训。
